sequence: for each row r = 0..511 (any order; rows are independent):
phase R (RESET): selected row line 0 V; word line r at V_WL; bitlines of the devices that must be HRS driven to V_RESET; all other bitlines at 0 V (= row level);
unselected row lines 0 / V/2, unselected word lines 0 V; apply pulse; switch to verify; read row r (160 columns, 1F read path);
retire the devices that verified; repeat with the 1D-ii amplitude/width schedule until all retired or N_max
phase S (SET):   selected row line V_SET; bitlines of the devices that must be LRS at 0 V; non-target bitlines at V_SET/2; unselected row lines 0 V,
unselected word lines 0 V; pulse; verify; retire; repeat
state the controller holds: the 160-bit weight row (gives both target masks: + device of a 1-cell / - device of a 0-cell), a 320-bit retired mask, the phase,
the iteration count (<= N_max, 1D-ii), the current pulse amplitude/width code (per row, or per device if the 1D-ii schedule is per device: 320 x a few bits),
the bias-level selects of the five line classes, and the mode (write / verify) with its switch-over timing
the a = 0 skip and group sequencing of the read path are not involved; programming is row-sequential

recal.item: per-group ladder thresholds (1C, 16,140 bits half table)
recal.depends_on: geometry + the POPULATION MEAN of the programmed LRS/HRS conductances (not individual cells)
recal.survives_reprogram: yes if the verify targets and their mean placement are unchanged; no if the targets or the program-verify bias move
recal.regenerate: measure the level of every (group, a, m) on reference patterns: 64 groups x 44 levels x 16 reads = 45,056 full-array reads

recal.depends_on: geometry (row line, rails) and the active-row count a; weights only through the data-dependent terms already in the budget
recal.regenerate: not needed; re-fit only if the rails/drivers change

recal.item: per-column front-end trims (1F, 2 x 2 x 10 bits per column = 6.4 kbit)
recal.depends_on: the sense front-end's own mismatch and temperature; NOT the cells
recal.survives_reprogram: yes (front-end property) - but it is FITTED through known cells, so it can only be re-fitted once the array holds known data
recal.regenerate: 18 known configurations (2 groups x m = 0..8) x 9 reads = 162 full-array reads per fit

recal.depends_on: front-end gain/offset drift 0.05 uA/K (1F) [+ the cell read-current TC if any: 1D-ii D3]
